newsitem.title: POLAND: Court registers Poland's Pekao banking group.
newsitem.headline: Court registers Poland's Pekao banking group.

text.p: A Warsaw court on Friday registered a banking group which emerged from a merger of four state-owned banks led by Bank Pekao SA, Pekao said.
The decision formally marks the launch of the group, created under a government scheme to strengthen the banking system and speed up privatisation of the four institutions, Pekao said in a statement.
In the group, which controls about 20 percent of Poland's banking sector, Pekao holds shares of Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA, Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA, and Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA.

The group hopes its privatisation could start late in 1997 with a sale of between 25 and 35 percent of its shares. The state treasury has yet to decide whether it would sell its stake or the group would issue new stock.
In June the four banks had a balance sheet total of 37 billion zlotys and own assets of two billion zlotys. Their share capital is 137.7 million zlotys.
